study.title: Simulation-informed learning for time-resolved angiographic contrast agent concentration reconstruction

imaging.modality_detail: Simulated rotational 4D-DSA projection images (DeepDRR forward projection of CFD-based contrast agent transport)
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebrovascular trees (ICA inlet, MCA, ACA); aneurysms removed

public_dataset_used.detail: AneuX morphology database surface meshes (plus in-house segmentations)

data_released.detail: Raw and processed data cannot be shared due to legal reasons

task.task_description: Learning-based reconstruction of spatially averaged, time-resolved (1D+T) contrast agent concentration at vessel centerline points from rotational angiographic projections, correcting vessel overlap and foreshortening artifacts; trained on CFD-based simulations.
task.clinical_application: Time-resolved 4D-DSA flow reconstruction for neurovascular hemodynamic assessment

temporal_evidence.quote: the spatial dimensions of the image can be interpreted as the distance along the centerline and time

metrics.metric: Mean absolute percentage error (mean +/- SD, abstract)
Coefficient of determination R2 (predicted vs ground truth)

code_available.detail: Code available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request

G1.quote: Previous works only qualitatively assessed the performance of their methods, making a direct comparison to our approach impossible.

G2.quote: our method was so far not evaluated on real angiographic projection images, for which image noise and out-of-distribution flow scenarios may lead to decreased model performance.

G3.quote: approximates the spatially averaged but time-resolved 1D+T CA concentration at all centerline points in the vasculature

G4.quote: However, due to the single view, 2D-DSA images are impaired by vascular overlay and vessel foreshortening, limiting their application for complex abnormalities.

G5.quote: One major advantage of the coupling of imaging and CFD simulations is the possibility to quantitatively evaluate 4D reconstruction algorithms, as real-world 4D contrast intensities cannot be measured with existing imaging modalities.

G7.quote: A combined estimation of CA concentrations and velocity fields could also improve interpretability and enables the computation of PDE residuals as a quality metric during inference.

other_limitations: Reduced-order 1D+T model not applicable to complex hemodynamics in aneurysms or AVMs
Contrast agent calibration required for application to real images
future_work: Phantom studies with CFD fitted to flow probe or Doppler ultrasound measurements
Patient-specific CFD with boundary conditions fitted from projection images
Combining the learning-based approach with CFD parameter optimization
Physics-informed neural networks to infer hidden hemodynamics from reconstructed concentrations
Higher-dimensional representations for complex pathologies such as aneurysms
Generalizability across acquisition protocols including static viewpoints
